headline: A domestic inflation shock lands on top of the Iran oil scare — PSX limps through a second choppy session while large banks and refiners hold up better than the rest of the tape.
summary: Pakistan's August inflation just shocked higher — 11.1% year-on-year, up from 9.2% in July — landing right as global oil stays elevated on the US-Iran standoff (Brent near $92, up 10% this month). That combination pushes any SBP rate cut off the table for the September 14 meeting and argues for a longer hawkish hold. PSX's last confirmed close was down 0.41% on August 31, and today's session has been choppy and unconfirmed as of this checkpoint. The desk is leaning cautious: sheltering in large banks riding high government-bond yields and refiners that actually gained on the oil move, and staying away from cement, autos, power and thinly-capitalized banks.

sectors.name: Banks (large-cap, government-paper holders)
sectors.why: The CPI shock kills near-term rate-cut hopes into the Sept 14 SBP meeting — bullish for the T-bill/PIB carry income these banks collect (6M T-bill 11.8%, 10Y PIB 12.3%), and most of the big names (BAFL, BAHL, BOP, HBL, MCB, NBP) screen 'attractive' on fundamentals.

sectors.name: Refineries (ATRL/PRL/NRL)
sectors.why: The one sector that actually gained on the Aug-31 sell-off — a higher Brent price widens refining crack spreads even though the same oil move hurts everyone else's import bill.

sectors.name: E&P (POL standout; OGDC/PPL/MARI broadly)
sectors.why: Higher crude directly lifts E&P revenue and georisk.json flags OGDC/PPL/MARI as beneficiaries, but their fundamentals only rate 'mixed' — POL's cheap valuation and near-10% dividend yield make it the cleaner expression of the same idea.

sectors.name: OMCs (PSO etc.)
sectors.why: Squeezed both ways — pump prices reset almost daily while the cost of the imported product itself is rising — and PSO's own net margin is thin, around 1%.

sectors.name: Cement, autos, power/IPPs
sectors.why: All three were named among the broad sellers on Aug-31, and power/IPPs carry the extra overhang of an unresolved circular-debt sticking point heading into the IMF's September review.

sectors.name: Small / thinly-capitalized banks
sectors.why: The CPI shock removes any near-term rate-relief story these names needed, and they lack the government-paper carry cushion the large banks have.

watchlist.angle: A golden-cross trend strategy is live on this name — a proven, backtested signal (strategy_map.json: 75% historical hit rate, 100% out-of-sample hit rate, net expectancy ~4.8%). Fundamentals back it up: PSX rates BAFL 'attractive', and it's a large bank riding the carry tailwind now that the CPI shock has pushed a near-term SBP cut off the table.
watchlist.risk: The run is already extended technically — a stall or reversal in the golden-cross setup would flip this from trend-following to chasing; also watch for a hawkish SBP surprise on Sept 14 that hits banks broadly.

watchlist.angle: Rated 'attractive' on fundamentals — a large, well-capitalized bank that fits the favoured sector tilt. It also has a live, dated catalyst right now: book closure running 2026-09-01 to 09-03 for a confirmed Rs3.5/share dividend.
watchlist.risk: No live technical trigger is backing this one — it's a fundamentals-and-catalyst case, not a chart-confirmed setup, so it can lag or chop even if the thesis holds.

watchlist.angle: Fresh 1HCY26 results just landed — profit up 44% YoY to about Rs9.37bn (impact-4 news, 2026-08-28). Fundamentals rate 'attractive' with a generous, covered dividend, and there's a dated catalyst: confirmed ex-dividend/book-closure on 2026-09-10/11 (Rs1.6/share, ~4.6% yield).
watchlist.risk: Higher beta than most banks (around 1.2 per the fundamental read) means it swings harder than the index both ways — a risk-off wobble hits BOP disproportionately.

watchlist.angle: Rated 'attractive' — cheap valuation (P/E ~6.2), a very strong profit margin, and one of the highest dividend yields on the board (~13.5%, payout ~84%). Sits in the E&P bucket that georisk.json flags as a direct beneficiary of the ongoing oil-price shock, plus a confirmed dated catalyst: ex-dividend/book-closure on 2026-10-12/13 (Rs72.5/share, ~9.9% yield).
watchlist.risk: No proven technical strategy is currently triggering on POL — this is a fundamentals-plus-catalyst case, not a chart-confirmed one — and a sharp Brent pullback, if the Iran standoff cools, would remove the sector tailwind fast.

watchlist.angle: The only name with two independently-matching technical confirmations: the desk's live signal feed and the strategy backtest file both show a Donchian-55 breakout ('turtle' style) triggering, net expectancy roughly 3.6-4.9% depending on the exact template, hit rate 61-70%.
watchlist.risk: Confidence tier is rated 'low' by the desk's own framework — small sample (13 trades) and no fundamental rating on file to back the story, so this is a pure technical, unconfirmed-by-fundamentals bet.

OGDC and PSO results due (unconfirmed date)
BOP ex-dividend / book-closure begins (09-11) — confirmed Rs1.6/share
SBP MPC — CPI now at 11.1%, near-term rate-cut odds effectively off the table
LUCK ex-dividend / book-closure begins (09-18) — confirmed Rs5.0/share
MARI ex-dividend/book-closure and INDU ex-dividend/book-closure both begin (09-22)
ATRL, APL, HUBC and POL ex-dividend/book-closure all begin (10-13)
IMF 4th EFF / 3rd RSF review mission expected — circular debt the key sticking point

risks: Inflation proves stickier than one print, or SBP surprises hawkish beyond a hold on Sept 14 — that breaks the bank-carry thesis this desk is leaning on today.
Further Strait of Hormuz escalation pushes Brent higher still, widening the import bill against a thin ~2.6-month reserve cushion ($17.1bn) and testing the PKR/DXY calm that has held so far.
The IMF's September review stalls on the circular-debt sticking point — a disappointment there would hit power/IPP-linked names hardest and sour sentiment across the board.
